    (hM13 : GeneralizedParabolicRescalingTheory.{u} n) :

tex_content.label: thm:ancient-structure
tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Structural estimates and normalization] For an ancient $\kappa $-solution, at every point and $t\leq 0$, \[ 0<R(t,x),\quad A(t,x)\leq R(t,x)\leq nA(t,x),\quad 0\leq \operatorname {Ric}(v,v)\leq Rg(v,v). \] For $s\leq t\leq 0$, \[ R(s,x)\leq R(t,x),\quad g(t)\leq g(s),\quad d_t\leq d_s,\quad B_s(p,r)\subseteq B_t(p,r). \] For each $b\leq 0$, $A$ is uniformly bounded on $N\times (-\infty ,b]$; indeed $A(t,x)\leq R(b,x)$ for $t\leq b$. For $p\in N$ and $Q=R(b,p)>0$, the same-carrier flow $\widehat g(s)=Qg(b+s/Q)$, $s\leq 0$, is an ancient solution with the same $\kappa $ and $\widehat R(0,p)=1$.

↗ def:ancient-kappa Source: MT2007 1. Theorem 4.40, p. 822. Definition 3.40, p. 613. Section 9.1
Proof

Curvature-operator positivity gives the tensor inequalities. The ancient trace Harnack inequality gives scalar monotonicity; its path form propagates positivity from a nonflat earlier slice. Integrating the Ricci-flow equation gives metric and distance monotonicity. The slice curvature bound at $b$ therefore controls every earlier time. Parabolic scaling multiplies lengths, volumes, and curvature by $\sqrt Q$, $Q^{n/2}$, and $Q^{-1}$, preserving the noncollapsing constant.

□
